question: Which statement best describes Declarative UI?
options: A component is a reusable piece of a page, such as a button or menu. It is like a building block: combine small blocks to make a larger page.
You say what the screen should show, and React works out how to update it. It is like telling a map your destination instead of giving every turn yourself.
Data usually moves from a parent component down to its children. This makes it easier to find where a value came from, like following a package from sender to recipient.

The virtual DOM is React's in-memory description of the page. React compares the old and new descriptions before changing the browser page, like checking two drafts and marking only the changed lines.
explanation: You say what the screen should show, and React works out how to update it. It is like telling a map your destination instead of giving every turn yourself.

question: Which statement best describes Components?
options: A component is a reusable piece of a page, such as a button or menu. It is like a building block: combine small blocks to make a larger page.
Data usually moves from a parent component down to its children. This makes it easier to find where a value came from, like following a package from sender to recipient.

The virtual DOM is React's in-memory description of the page. React compares the old and new descriptions before changing the browser page, like checking two drafts and marking only the changed lines.
Reconciliation is how React decides which visible parts need updating. It compares the previous screen description with the new one, much like spotting differences between two photos.
explanation: A component is a reusable piece of a page, such as a button or menu. It is like a building block: combine small blocks to make a larger page.
